title: Introduction to venous thromboembolism and antithrombotic drugs

units.name: Introduction: venous thromboembolism
units.assessment: Can you say roughly how often VTE occurs, in whom the burden falls hardest, and separate low-risk, intermediate-risk and high-risk pulmonary embolism by the clinical, imaging and biomarker findings that define each band?

lesson.title: 2020 ASSH Seminar 1: Venous Thromboembolism
lesson.why: A single hour-long haematology seminar that walks the whole VTE story end to end - burden, presentation, DVT versus PE, and how severity drives the initial treatment decision.

drills.name: ASH guideline treatment recommendations
drills.title: Treatment | ASH Clinical Practice Guidelines on Venous Thromboembolism (VTE)

drills.name: The population burden of VTE
drills.title: Venous Thromboembolism: "A Public Health Concern"

units.name: The pathophysiology of venous thrombosis
units.assessment: Can you name the three arms of Virchow's triad and give, for each, a concrete clinical setting that drives thrombus formation in the valve pocket of a deep vein rather than in an artery?

lesson.title: Overview of Thrombosis & Treatment
lesson.why: A clinician-level overview that builds venous thrombosis from stasis, endothelial injury and hypercoagulability before moving to treatment, which is exactly the arc of this section.

drills.name: Thrombus formation animated
drills.title: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Pathology

units.name: Diagnosis of VTE
units.assessment: For a patient with suspected DVT or PE, can you state how pretest probability scoring, D-dimer and imaging fit together, and identify the combinations that let you safely stop without any imaging at all?

lesson.title: VTE Diagnosis in the Emergency Department
lesson.why: A dedicated 45-minute talk on the diagnostic pathway as it is actually run - Wells scoring, age-adjusted D-dimer thresholds, and when to go to CTPA or compression ultrasound.

drills.name: Diagnostic pitfalls and misconceptions
drills.title: Misconceptions in diagnosis of VTE - Prof Beverley Hunt OBE

drills.name: ASH guideline diagnostic recommendations
drills.title: Diagnosing VTE | ASH Clinical Practice Guidelines on Venous Thromboembolism

units.name: Recurrent VTE despite anticoagulant treatment
units.assessment: If a patient clots again while on therapeutic anticoagulation, can you work through the differential - adherence, absorption and dosing, occult malignancy, antiphospholipid antibodies, HIT - and say what you would change about the regimen?

lesson.title: ISTH Academy Presentation: Anticoagulant Therapy in the Treatment of Venous Thromboembolism
lesson.why: An ISTH Academy talk on anticoagulant therapy for VTE that frames treatment failure and how the choice of agent and intensity is revisited when a patient breaks through.

drills.name: The exact bedside scenario
drills.title: In the Trenches: Recurrent DVT Despite Therapeutic Anticoagulation

drills.name: Quantifying recurrence risk
drills.title: Risk of Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism

units.name: Duration of anticoagulant therapy
units.assessment: Can you decide whether a given VTE earns three months, extended or indefinite anticoagulation, and explain how provoked-versus-unprovoked status, the site of the clot and bleeding risk each push that decision?

lesson.title: Duration of Anticoagulation Treatment - Case Study
lesson.why: A case-based Thrombosis Canada session built specifically around the stop-or-continue decision, which is the whole content of this section.

drills.title: Oral anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs in the secondary prevention of venous thromboembolism

units.name: Postthrombotic syndrome
units.assessment: Can you describe how postthrombotic syndrome presents, how the Villalta score grades it, and what the randomized evidence actually shows for compression stockings and for catheter-directed thrombolysis as prevention?

lesson.title: Post thrombotic syndrome- Intervention
lesson.why: A Thrombosis UK session devoted to postthrombotic syndrome and the interventional options, rather than treating it as a footnote to DVT management.

units.name: Antithrombotic drugs
units.assessment: For each class of antithrombotic - factor Xa inhibitor DOAC, direct thrombin inhibitor, LMWH, fondaparinux, UFH - can you state its target, onset, renal handling, monitoring assay and the reversal strategy you would use in a bleeding patient?

lesson.title: What's New in Antithrombotic Treatment of VTE Disease: ACCP (CHEST) Guidelines Update 2021
lesson.why: An Anticoagulation Forum review of the CHEST guideline update that goes agent by agent through the antithrombotics used in VTE and where each one belongs.

units.assessment: Can you explain why warfarin is not antithrombotic for several days, which vitamin K-dependent factors fall first and why that matters for skin necrosis, and how you would manage a supratherapeutic INR with and without bleeding?

lesson.title: Vitamin K antagonists
lesson.why: A tight coagulation-focused explainer on how vitamin K antagonists work, what the INR is really measuring and where the pitfalls in monitoring sit.

lesson.why: Jim Douketis takes the special-population problems - renal failure, obesity, procedures, bleeding - that make up this section and gives a practical rule for each.
